title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 119
paragraphs: After this, when the Persians had come and crossed the Maeander, the Carians engaged them at the river Marsyas and fought a battle that was stubbornly contested and long, but in the end they were worsted by superior numbers. Of the Persians some two thousand fell, but of the Carians ten thousand. Those who escaped were shut up in Labraunda within the sanctuary of Zeus Stratius, a great sacred grove of plane-trees (the Carians are the only people we know of who sacrifice to Zeus Stratius). These men, shut up there, were taking counsel among themselves about their safety—whether they would fare better by surrendering to the Persians or by leaving Asia altogether.
